source: Candidate CVFR green-route altitude scaffold. Coordinates are not duplicated here; segment endpoint ids resolve against docs/data/cvfr-nav-waypoints.json and docs/data/airfields.json. Some rows were detected from CVFR chart imagery and manually audited; sibling coverage rows with source=cvfr-map airway adjacency were seeded from the upstream airway table so direct CVFR legs are visible in the editable chart. Candidate altitudes should be checked against official CVFR chart labels before promotion. Double-ended same-route markers may apply the same altitude both directions, while one-way routes use null for the disallowed direction. status=reviewed marks rows confirmed from maintainer-provided evidence. status=unknown with two null altitudes is an editable placeholder.

schema.segments: Candidate direct green CVFR route segments. Endpoint coordinates are looked up by from/to in docs/data/cvfr-nav-waypoints.json or docs/data/airfields.json. inboundAltitude is from -> to; outboundAltitude is to -> from. Altitudes are feet MSL. A single null means that direction is not allowed and requires oneWay=true; two nulls require status=unknown and mean the row is an editable placeholder. Candidate values may come from chart-read yellow CVFR altitude arrows/markers or from source=cvfr-map airway adjacency sibling coverage. Double-ended same-route markers may apply the same altitude both directions. status=reviewed marks rows confirmed from maintainer-provided evidence.

commMeta.source: Comm-change reporting points populated from maintainer visual inspection of the printed IAA CVFR chart symbology ('נקודת מעבר קשר' — comm-transfer point legend), 2026-05-31, with a full waypoint tile audit follow-up on 2026-06-17. Call-sign frequency options are enriched from the maintainer-provided AirMapRadioFrequencies PDF generated 2026-06-06; assign available options per waypoint in points[].callSigns. Earlier desk-research sources (Israel eAIP 2025-10-02, PAMAT edition 1/24) did not yield OCR-extractable per-point data — see _NOTE.
commMeta._definition: Each entry marks a CVFR reporting point where pilots are expected to switch ATC frequencies because the point sits on (or at) a sector / CTR / TMA boundary. The chart annotation may be on the boundary line itself rather than directly at the point — the dataset records the *point of change*, not the chart-text position.
commMeta._NOTE: Reporting-type (חובה / דרישה — mandatory vs. on-request) is NOT comm-change and is tracked separately (PR #405). The points below come from maintainer inspection of the printed IAA CVFR chart's 'נקודת מעבר קשר' symbology, which supersedes the earlier citation bar that left this file empty. Points are matched to cvfr-nav-waypoints.json by 5-letter ICAO `name` only — never by Hebrew text.
commMeta._callSignsUsage: Root callSigns is the reusable frequency catalog. Add call-sign ids to a comm-change waypoint's points[].callSigns array to expose those choices in the frequency-callout inspector. Optional points[].routeHints entries map route context to a call-sign id from that same point's callSigns array: before/after are adjacent route waypoint names around the comm-change point, and callSign is the suggested frequency owner. Labels/frequencies are derived from the catalog. The first id becomes the default; the frequency remains editable on the note.
